To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
two distinct mechanisms for adenine nucleotide exchange are present in mitochondria of kidney cortex.

the adenine nucleotide content of isolated kidney cortex mitochondria is 8.2 nmol/mg protein and that net transport of adenine nucleotide occurs by a mechanism that catalyzing net transfer of adenines across the inner membrane.

the adenine nucleotide (ATP +ADP +AMP) content of isolated rat kidney mitochondria can increase or decrease as a function of external [ATP], that these changes occur by a transport process that is sensitive to EGTA and carboxyatracyloside (CAT) and that this transport process can be characterized as two distinct mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of adenine nucleotide metabolism in rat kidney mitochondrias.
the regulation of the mitochondrial adenine nucleotide pool.
the role of the adenine nucleotide translocase in the regulation of mitochondrial energy metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAT-insensitive adenylate carrier in rat kidney mitochondrion is a phosphate carrier, and the CAT-sensitive adenylate carrier is an ADP/ATp translocase.

the CAT-insensitive adeninenucleotide transport is identical to the adeninenucleotidetranslocase and that the CAT-sensitive adeninenucleo tide transport is identical to an adeninenucleoside carrier that is not present or active in liver mitochondria.
there are at least 2 distinct transport systems in the mitochondrial inner membrane for the net transfer of adenyl nucleotides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
net adenine nucleotide flux in kidney mitochondria is mediated by two transport mechanisms.

there are at least three adenine nucleotide carriers in the inner mitochondrial membrane: the adenine nucleoside translocase, the CAT-insensitive adeninenucleotide/ Pi carrier, and the CAT-sensitive adenine nucleotide/Pi carrier.
net adenine nucleotide transport occurs in kidney mitochondria by two mechanisms, one identical to that in liver and the other unique to kidney.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kidney mitochondria have two distinct mechanisms for ATP transport.
the adenine nucleotide transport system in kidney mitochondria has two components.
the adenine nucleotide pool of kidney mitochondria is not only controlled by adenine nucleotide synthesis and hydrolysis but also regulated by net transport.
